Briefly, EED was incubated with 10 mM B-nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide hydrate, 2 mM of a tightly binding proprietary compound, and 0.5 mM of a synthesized peptide which comprises the helix on EZH2 which interacts with EED. The crystals were grown using the vapor diffusion method. One uL of the protein mixture was combined with 1 uL of a precipitant comprised of 20% (w/v) PEG3350, 0.2 M potassium iodide, and 0.1M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5, on a cover slip which was  suspended over a reservoir comprised of 0.5 mL of precipitant at 18 Celsius and sealed. The crystals grew in 4-6 days at 18 Celsius and then harvested and soaked in defined drops consisting of 30 uL of precipitant and 2 mM of compound for 24 h. Crystals were cryopreserved for data collection using a cryosolution consisting of 30% PEG 400 (v/v), 20% (w/v) PEG 3350, 0.2 M potassium iodide, and 0.1M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5

Once holoenzyme crystals reached their maximum size within seven days, 1 uL of 10 mM GABA was added to the drop with crystals. After soaking, crystals were transferred into a cryoprotective solution (well solution supplemented with 30% glycerol), and then flash-frozen in liquid nitrogen.
